We have  
\[
f(z)=az+b,\quad a=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2},\quad b=-\sqrt3-9i.
\]
For a rotation about \(c\),
\[
f(z)=a(z-c)+c=az+(1-a)c,
\]
so
\[
b=(1-a)c \quad\Rightarrow\quad c=\frac{b}{1-a}.
\]
Now
\[
1-a=\frac{3-i\sqrt3}{2},
\]
hence
\[
c=\frac{-\sqrt3-9i}{\frac{3-i\sqrt3}{2}}
=\frac{2(-\sqrt3-9i)}{3-i\sqrt3}.
\]
Multiplying by the conjugate \(3+i\sqrt3\),
\[
c=\frac{2(-\sqrt3-9i)(3+i\sqrt3)}{12}
=\frac{(-\sqrt3-9i)(3+i\sqrt3)}{6}.
\]
Expanding,
\[
(-\sqrt3-9i)(3+i\sqrt3)=6\sqrt3-30i,
\]
so
\[
c=\frac{6\sqrt3-30i}{6}=\sqrt3-5i.
\]

The answer is \(\sqrt3-5i\).

We have  
\[
f(z)=\frac{(-1+i\sqrt3)z+(-2\sqrt3-18i)}{2}.
\]
A rotation about center \(c\) has the form  
\[
f(z)=a(z-c)+c,
\]
where \(|a|=1\). Here the coefficient of \(z\) is  
\[
a=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Indeed \(|a|=1\), so this is a rotation.

Write  
\[
f(z)=az+b,
\]
where  
\[
b=\frac{-2\sqrt3-18i}{2}=-\sqrt3-9i.
\]
For a rotation about \(c\),  
\[
f(z)=a(z-c)+c=az+(1-a)c.
\]
Thus  
\[
b=(1-a)c.
\]
So  
\[
c=\frac{b}{1-a}.
\]

Compute  
\[
1-a=1-\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}
=\frac{2+1-i\sqrt3}{2}
=\frac{3-i\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Therefore  
\[
c=\frac{-\sqrt3-9i}{\frac{3-i\sqrt3}{2}}
=\frac{2(-\sqrt3-9i)}{3-i\sqrt3}.
\]
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(3+i\sqrt3\):
\[
c=\frac{2(-\sqrt3-9i)(3+i\sqrt3)}{9+3}.
\]
The denominator is \(12\), so
\[
c=\frac{(-\sqrt3-9i)(3+i\sqrt3)}{6}.
\]
Now expand:
\[
(-\sqrt3)(3)=-3\sqrt3,\quad
(-\sqrt3)(i\sqrt3)=-3i,
\]
\[
(-9i)(3)=-27i,\quad
(-9i)(i\sqrt3)=9\sqrt3.
\]
So the product is
\[
(-3\sqrt3+9\sqrt3)+(-3i-27i)
=6\sqrt3-30i.
\]
Thus
\[
c=\frac{6\sqrt3-30i}{6}=\sqrt3-5i.
\]

The answer is \(\sqrt3-5i\).
